title: Optimize walkthrough - quantization profiles (INT8 / FP8)
next_steps: Sarah to share quantization profiles deck and benchmark spreadsheet by 2025-06-27
Customer to provide 3 representative prompt sets and a tail latency SLO by 2025-07-02
Schedule follow-up POC kickoff (benchmark run) week of 2025-07-07
action_items: Sarah Kim: share quant profiles deck + spreadsheet by 2025-06-27
Marcus Li: upload 3 prompt sets and baseline perf logs by 2025-07-01
Javier Morales: prepare test harness and run initial INT8/FP8 A/B benchmark during POC
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Acme Financial through Redwood Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8). Discussed quality vs latency tradeoffs, expected token-cost reductions, recommended evaluation metrics, and next steps for a POC benchmark using 3 prompt sets. Security and deployment questions covered (VPC/KMS, dedicated vs hosted).
topics: Optimize walkthrough, quantization profiles, INT8, FP8, quality vs latency, batching, KV cache, benchmark plan, POC next steps, security requirements
transcript:
00:00:05 Sarah: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna walk through Redwood Optimize quantization profiles today, slide deck in the chat, and then we'll get into some numbers, and then a plan for POC.
00:00:17 Priya: hi yeah thanks, quick note we have limited time so mostly want to focus on quality regressions and tail latency, those are our main blockers for production.
00:00:29 Javier: got it, we'll keep an eye on those. Quick intro - I'm Javier, performance SE - I'll show some live numbers and a sample benchmark approach.
00:00:40 Marcus: thanks, Marcus here, ML infra, mostly curious how INT8 and FP8 behave on our longer context prompts, we often hit 8k windows with KV cache in production.
00:00:52 Sarah: perfect, so agenda: recap what quant profiles are in Redwood Optimize, show INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, quality vs latency charts, and then POC next steps.
00:01:12 Sarah: quick aside, these profiles are what our optimize engine suggests - it's not an automatic black box, you can pin and roll back.
00:01:22 Daniel: is the quantization happening in the serving runtime or during compilation? like, where does the FP8-ish path live?
00:01:31 Javier: good question, it's in the runtime: we pick kernels at compile and runtime that support INT8/FP8 paths, and there is a fallback to FP16 if a pattern isn't supported. sometimes the notes in the docs spell it out as f-p eight and int eight so transcriptions can be weird.
00:01:50 Priya: can you give a quick example of quality delta? numbers please.
00:01:56 Javier: yep - on a 7B-class model we tested, INT8 typically reduced per-token compute by ~2.6x vs FP16 and latency 30-40% lower in steady state; FP8 gave ~1.8-2.0x compute reduction and latency 20-30% lower. Quality: INT8 had a small measurable degradation on certain instruction-following prompts - think 1-3% drop on our rouge/accuracy slices - FP8 had smaller degradation, often sub-1% on those slices.
00:02:30 Marcus: those numbers look promising, but what's the variance on long context? our tails blow up when KV cache isn't warm.
00:02:36 Javier: tail latency is mostly affected by cold cache and very long prefix recompute. For cold starts INT8 helps less because memory bandwidth and kernel setup dominate, FP8 tends to be slightly better for tails because it preserves more numeric fidelity and thus needs fewer retries for beam ops. but again, depends on model and tokenizer mix.
00:02:55 Aisha: sorry interrupt, when you say 'retries for beam ops' do you mean fallback to higher precision mid-request?
00:03:02 Javier: yeah like if we detect numerical instability we can fallback certain layers to higher precision (FP16) for that request - it's controlled by the quant profile policy. that's part of Redwood's graceful degradation.
00:03:18 Sarah: and that's configurable in the console under Optimize -> Quant Profiles; you can tune thresholds and set auto-rollbacks.
00:03:27 Priya: security question - if we use dedicated vs hosted, does quantization affect data residency or encryption keys?
00:03:36 Sarah: quantization itself is compute level; it doesn't change KMS or audit logs. For Private/Dedicated deployments you bring your KMS and we still write audit logs the same way. We'll share the security pack.
00:03:49 Daniel: will quantization change our ability to repro outputs for compliance? we need deterministic reproductions for some audits.
00:03:57 Javier: good point - INT8 can introduce non-determinism if kernels use stochastic rounding or different vectorized paths; we have a deterministic mode that pins kernels and disables certain speedups for compliance runs (costlier). We'll note that in the action items.
00:04:15 Marcus: can we see an example trace? maybe a latency breakdown per token with and without quant?
00:04:22 Javier: yes - pulling up the slide: (link) - here's a waterfall: tokenization ~3-8ms, KV cache lookup 1-2ms, attention compute 12ms FP16 vs 5ms INT8 on this hardware, decode/new token generation 6ms. These are illustrative on A100-40Gb; on 80GB Vram or H100 numbers skew.
00:04:48 Priya: hardware question: we run on in-house A100s, any guidance on FP8 support on A100 vs H100?
00:04:56 Javier: FP8 benefits are most pronounced on H100 where the hardware kernels are optimized; A100 still sees gains for INT8 but FP8 paths are less mature, you may see only marginal improvements. We recommend INT8 on A100 for now.
00:05:12 Sarah: point about cost - INT8 reduces GPU hours per token and thus unit cost, but you have to check quality delta per your critical prompt sets.
00:05:20 Marcus: what about embeddings? we use embeddings for semantic search, can't tolerate quality drops there.
00:05:25 Javier: embeddings are sensitive; for those we usually recommend FP16 or a conservative FP8 profile with no layer quantization on the embedding head. Optimize can create separate profiles per route - e.g., embeddings route pinned to FP16.
00:05:40 Aisha: nice, route-level profiles are critical for us.
00:05:44 Sarah: demo time - I'll hand to Javier to show the console and the benchmark sheet.
00:05:50 Speaker 1: [screen share noise] OK uh sorry there's a little lag - lemme refresh -
00:06:05 Javier: Alright on the console, here is Optimize -> Quant Profiles, you can see prebuilt profiles: conservative-fp8, default-int8, aggressive-int8, and a per-route override area. I'll start an inline benchmark example.
00:06:20 Marcus: can the inline benchmark run against our private models or only Redwoods hosted models?
00:06:25 Javier: for Private/Dedicated we can run the same harness against your endpoints, we just need credentials and network access in the POC. For hosted you can use sample models or Redwood-managed replicas.
00:06:38 Sarah: note - for the POC we usually run a 48-hour A/B with sticky hashing and collect quality metrics plus tail percentiles.
00:06:47 Priya: sticky hashing? clarify.
00:06:50 Javier: it's our routing policy to ensure user sessions hit the same quant profile variant to avoid confounding. otherwise results mix.
00:06:59 Daniel: on the POC credentials - we prefer VPC peering and a dedicated subnet, not open endpoints.
00:07:05 Sarah: that's fine, we'll propose a dedicated VPC peering for the POC. Action wise we'll include configuration steps in the next email.
00:07:14 Marcus: can you explain 'aggressive-int8' differences? what layers get quantized?
00:07:19 Javier: aggressive quantizes most matmuls and some attention projections, conservative only quantizes feedforward matmuls leaving attention in FP16, and the profile includes layer exceptions per-model. We'll share the exact layer map in the spreadsheet.
00:07:33 Priya: what's the rollback strategy if we see quality regressions mid-run?
00:07:37 Javier: auto-rollback can be set to trigger on precomputed evaluation thresholds or on manual review. We can also run per-batch golden prompts and if the error rate exceeds X% we revert.
00:07:49 Aisha: what's X typically?
00:07:51 Sarah: teams pick X; we suggest 2% for user-facing generative prompts, and 0.5% for critical regulatory outputs.
00:07:59 Marcus: are you collecting token-level diffs to help debug quality regressions?
00:08:04 Javier: yes the benchmark sheet has diffs, perplexity, rouge-like scores and also a sample trace with token logits for failing cases - that helps SEs triage which layers or ops cause drift.
00:08:19 Priya: ok sounds good. curious about concurrency - if we increase batching to save cost does quantization interact badly with batch sizes?
00:08:29 Javier: batching and quantization interact in two ways: larger batches improve throughput but can amplify quantization noise for some ops; and also memory layout matters. Optimize suggests batch size heuristics per-profile. In practice we tune jointly: small batch low latency, medium batch plus INT8 for throughput.
00:08:49 Daniel: any gotchas with FP8 and mixed precision math for our reproducibility tests?
00:08:54 Javier: yes FP8 can be non-deterministic across different driver versions; lock CUDA/cuDNN versions in POC and enable deterministic mode for compliance runs.
00:09:05 Sarah: let's walk through a sample POC plan - step 1: customer provides 3 prompt sets (chat, long-context, embeddings). Step 2: Redwood runs a 48-72hr A/B across profiles INT8/FP8/FP16. Step 3: collect perf + quality metrics and then a joint review.
00:09:25 Priya: timeline? we have audit windows end of July so would like a POC start early July.
00:09:30 Sarah: we can start week of July 7th, that fits.
00:09:35 Marcus: small nit, in your earlier slides you showed INT8 giving 30-40% lower latency - is that p50 or p95?
00:09:41 Javier: those headline were p50-ish; p95 improvements are smaller - more like 10-25% depending on cache warmness and model. p99 could be close to baseline if there's heavy I/O.
00:09:56 Priya: can you send us the exact metrics you collect? we need p50/p95/p99, mean tokens/sec, failure rate, and quality slices.
00:10:04 Sarah: will do - sending benchmark schema and sheet.
00:10:10 Speaker 2: [background] can you paste the security link in the chat?
00:10:15 Sarah: pasted: security pack link.
00:10:20 Priya: thanks. another question - in some tests we saw hallucination increases with lower precision, what's your mitigation?
00:10:28 Javier: hallucination is often data/model related, but quantization can change token probabilities. Mitigations: 1) conservative profiles for instruction prompts, 2) layer exceptions on the LM head, 3) post-filtering and reranking using a higher precision model for critical outputs, 4) prompt engineering and calibration.
00:10:47 Marcus: reranking sounds expensive but maybe we can rerank only top-K on critical paths.
00:10:51 Javier: exactly, route-level policies let you do that only for money transfer flows, etc.
00:10:58 Aisha: any reference customers done FP8 in prod?
00:11:02 Sarah: a few - we can share anonymized perf slides, but most early FP8 adopters are on H100 clusters and have heavy throughput needs. We'll include references with NDA if needed.
00:11:14 Priya: thanks.
00:11:17 Sarah: ok we're nearing end, quick recap and next steps: action items... (see action_items). Questions?
00:11:27 Marcus: none from me, thanks.
00:11:30 Daniel: none.
00:11:33 Priya: thanks all, look forward to the POC plan.
00:11:37 Sarah: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet, deck and POC dates. bye.
00:11:45 [call ends]
